objectives: Outline NLP tasks on clinical text.

slides.title: Clinical text: the rich substrate
slides.body:
**80%+ of EHR information is in free text**: progress notes, discharge summaries, radiology + pathology reports, operative notes, consultations.

Structured fields are sparse + biased; the real clinical reasoning lives in narrative.

**Clinical NLP tasks**:
- **Named-entity recognition (NER)**: identify mentions of diseases, drugs, anatomy, labs, etc.
- **Concept normalization**: map mentions to standard terminologies (UMLS, SNOMED). E.g., 'high blood pressure' → C0020538 (UMLS CUI for Hypertension).
- **Negation + uncertainty + family-history detection**: 'no chest pain' ≠ 'chest pain'. 'Mother had MI' ≠ patient. NegEx, ConText algorithms.
- **Relation extraction**: drug-dose, drug-route, anatomy-finding, temporal relationships.
- **Coreference resolution**: 'the patient', 'she', 'this 65-year-old female'.
- **Section identification**: HPI, Past Medical, Medications, Labs, Assessment + Plan.
- **De-identification**: remove PHI (names, dates, addresses, MRNs, etc.).
- **Summarization**: long notes → key findings + plan.
- **Question answering**: 'What was the patient's most recent ejection fraction?'
- **Report generation**: image → text. Discharge → patient letter.

**Historical NLP tools**:
- **MetaMap** (NLM): UMLS concept extraction. Rule-based.
- **cTAKES** (Apache UIMA): clinical NLP pipeline.
- **CLAMP** (UTHealth): de-id + NER.
- **MedSpaCy**: clinical extensions to spaCy.
- **NegEx, ConText, pyConText**: negation/uncertainty.

**Embeddings + BERT-era**:
- **BioBERT** (2019): PubMed-pretrained BERT.
- **ClinicalBERT, Bio_ClinicalBERT**: MIMIC-pretrained.
- **PubMedBERT**: from-scratch on biomedical text.
- **GatorTron** (UF + NVIDIA): trained on hospital notes.
- **SciFive, BioGPT**: T5 + GPT variants.

**LLM era (2022+)**:
- **Med-PaLM 2, Med-PaLM M**: Google. Strong medical QA.
- **GPT-4, Claude, Gemini**: general LLMs achieving high scores on USMLE + medical benchmarks.
- **Open clinical LLMs**: Meditron, BioMistral, OpenBioLLM. Fine-tuned from Llama/Mistral.
- **Domain-specific apps**: Doximity (note summarization), Abridge + Augmedix + Suki + Nuance DAX (ambient scribing), Glass Health.

**Ambient AI scribes**: transcribe doctor-patient conversation → generate clinical note. Major active deployment in 2024. Nuance DAX, Abridge, Augmedix, Suki, Heidi Health, Microsoft's recent integrations.

Clinician time savings: ~1-2 hours/day. Major workflow + burnout reduction. Adoption growing rapidly.

slides.title: De-identification + privacy + LLM challenges
slides.body:
**De-identification (de-ID)**: remove or replace PHI to enable research + AI.

**HIPAA Safe Harbor** (USA): 18 identifiers must be removed.
- Names, geographic subdivisions smaller than state, dates (except year if not narrow age), phones, emails, SSNs, MRNs, account #s, vehicle IDs, devices, URLs, IPs, biometric IDs, photos, etc.
- Ages > 89 must be aggregated.
- After removal: considered de-identified.

**Expert Determination**: alternative statistical method. Confirm low re-identification risk. Allows retaining more useful info (e.g., specific dates).

**Synthetic identifiers**: replace real names/dates with consistent fake ones (preserve longitudinal structure).

**Automatic de-ID**:
- Tools: NLM Scrubber, Philter, Microsoft Presidio (general), MIST.
- LLM-based: GPT/Claude can de-ID well; concerns about accuracy + sending PHI to APIs.
- Performance: ~95-98% recall for major identifiers. Residual risk.
- Variability: rare names + creative writing harder.

**Re-identification risks**:
- Quasi-identifiers (rare diagnosis + zip code + age) can be linked to public data.
- Sweeney 2000: 87% of USA population uniquely identifiable by zip + DOB + sex.
- ML models can MEMORIZE training data (extraction attacks). Mitigation: differential privacy.

**Differential privacy in clinical ML**: noise added during training to bound re-identification. Trade-off: more privacy = less utility. Active research.

**Federated learning**: train across hospitals without sharing raw data. Models aggregated; local data stays local. NVIDIA FLARE, OpenFL frameworks. Used in EXAM consortium (COVID), MELLODDY (drug discovery).

**LLMs + clinical data challenges**:
- **API services + PHI**: sending PHI to OpenAI / Anthropic requires BAA (Business Associate Agreement) — available but legally + technically careful.
- **On-premise deployment**: open-weights models (Llama-3, Mistral, Qwen) deployed in hospital infrastructure.
- **Hallucination in medical text**: critical safety issue. LLM confidently invents lab values or drug doses.
- **Bias**: training data may underrepresent minorities or specific conditions.
- **Validation**: clinical use requires rigorous evaluation, ideally prospective.
- **Regulation**: FDA hasn't yet approved an LLM as a SaMD; pathways evolving.

**Modern clinical NLP applications**:
- **Note generation**: ambient + structured. The biggest 2023-2024 deployment.
- **Clinical decision support**: chat with patient chart.
- **Coding + billing**: automate ICD/CPT coding from notes.
- **Prior authorization**: automate insurance approval workflows.
- **Phenotype extraction**: identify cohorts for research.
- **Adverse event detection**: from notes for pharmacovigilance.
- **Patient communication**: simplify discharge instructions, translate.
- **Trial matching**: identify candidates for clinical trials.

slides.title: Validation + deployment + the modern clinical LLM stack
slides.body:
**Evaluating clinical LLMs**:

**Knowledge benchmarks**:
- USMLE (USA medical licensing): GPT-4 surpassed passing threshold in 2023; Med-PaLM 2 + others approaching human expert.
- MultiMedQA: composite QA benchmark (MedQA, PubMedQA, etc.).
- MedMCQA: India medical entrance exam.
- HealthBench (OpenAI 2024): rubric-based real-world clinical conversations.

**Real-world tasks**:
- Summarization quality vs reference summaries.
- Clinical accuracy (hallucination rate).
- Helpfulness (clinician ratings).
- Safety (avoid dangerous advice).

**Limitations of benchmarks**:
- Knowledge != judgment. Passing USMLE ≠ being good doctor.
- Doesn't capture interpersonal, longitudinal, multimodal aspects.
- Benchmarks may be in training data (contamination).
- Real clinical work is ambiguous + requires action.

**Clinical LLM evaluation frameworks** (active research):
- **TRIPOD-LLM, CONSORT-AI**: extensions of reporting standards for AI.
- **HEAL framework** (Google): equity-focused.
- **AHRQ Common Formats** for AE reporting.

**Deployment patterns**:
- **Embedded in EHR**: tool launches in Epic/Cerner; clinician interacts within workflow.
- **Sidecar tools**: separate UI consulting EHR via FHIR.
- **Mobile scribes**: phone-based ambient recording + note generation.
- **Patient-facing**: chatbot for triage, education, symptom checker. (Mostly outside FDA oversight at present.)

**Liability + medico-legal**:
- AI as 'decision-support': clinician retains responsibility.
- AI as 'autonomous': much higher bar (FDA approval, malpractice insurance).
- Recent FDA + state guidance evolving.
- Common practice: AI suggests, human approves.

**Implementation science**:
- Adoption requires more than 'good model': workflow fit, training, support, incentives.
- Champions, governance, change management.
- 'AI scribes' have rapid adoption because they SAVE TIME without changing clinical decisions.
- Decision support tools have slower adoption — clinicians wary of liability + workflow disruption.

**Modern clinical LLM stack** (typical 2024 deployment):
- Foundation model: GPT-4o/Claude/Gemini (API) or Llama/Mistral (on-prem).
- RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): pull from patient chart + medical knowledge bases.
- Guardrails: hallucination detection, safety filters.
- Audit logs: every interaction.
- Feedback loop: clinician corrections refine prompts/fine-tunes.

**Ethical considerations**:
- Informed consent: patients aware that AI is involved.
- Transparency about AI capabilities + limitations.
- Accountability: who's responsible for outcomes?
- Equity: AI must not amplify health disparities.
- Privacy: PHI handling.

**Future trajectories**:
- Multimodal clinical AI (image + text + audio + structured).
- Longitudinal patient digital twins.
- Clinician-AI collaboration patterns.
- Patient-facing AI for triage + education.
- Drug discovery via clinical AI.

question.question: Extract concepts from a clinical note
question.goal: Note: '67M with HTN, T2DM on metformin presents with SOB for 2 days. Denies chest pain. PMHx CAD s/p PCI 2019.'

options: HTN (hypertension), T2DM (type 2 diabetes), metformin (medication), SOB (shortness of breath), chest pain (NEGATED), CAD (coronary artery disease), PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention, dated 2019).

steps.reveal: Entities: HTN, T2DM, metformin, SOB, chest pain (negated!), CAD, PCI 2019. Each maps to UMLS/SNOMED. Key: 'denies chest pain' must be NEGATED — not flagged as a positive finding.

steps.prompt: Why is negation detection critical clinically?

options: Failing to recognize negation causes false-positive findings. 'Denies chest pain' wrongly extracted as 'chest pain present' would change AI risk score + alert workflows. NegEx + ConText algorithms (Chapman 2001) detect negation, uncertainty, family history.

steps.reveal: Negation detection critical: 'denies chest pain' ≠ chest pain. Missing negation = false positive findings = wrong clinical conclusions. NegEx + ConText algorithms + modern transformer-based negation classifiers achieve ~95% accuracy.

steps.prompt: Modern LLM-based extraction (GPT-4, Claude) vs rule-based (cTAKES). Trade-offs?

options: LLMs: higher accuracy on complex/ambiguous text, handles abbreviations + jargon + grammar variations, generalizable to new entity types. Rule-based: predictable, explainable, fast, no PHI to external API needed. Hybrid often best.

steps.reveal: LLMs more accurate but: PHI to API or expensive on-prem; less explainable; hallucination risk. Rule-based: deterministic + auditable + free + local. Hybrid: rules for structured/critical fields, LLMs for messy free text. Modern stacks combine.

question.finalResult: $$\boxed{\text{Clinical NLP: NER + normalization + negation + temporality + sectioning}}$$ The pipeline is mature but ever-evolving. Foundation models (Med-PaLM 2, GPT-4, Claude) achieve high accuracy on most tasks but require careful evaluation + PHI handling. Hybrid systems (rules + LLMs) common in production. 2024 hot topic: AI scribes generating notes from doctor-patient conversations — the largest active deployment of clinical NLP.

question.question: AI medical scribes (Nuance DAX, Abridge, Augmedix, Suki, Heidi Health) are rapidly deploying in 2024. Why such fast adoption?
options: Save clinicians 1-2 hours/day of documentation work. Reduce burnout. Don't change clinical decisions (so lower regulatory + medico-legal risk). Clinicians experience direct benefit. Hospitals see throughput + retention gains. Aligned incentives → rapid adoption.
question.explanation:
AI scribes capture doctor-patient conversation + draft a clinical note. Clinician reviews + signs. Saves ~1-2 hours/day documentation. Burnout is a major industry problem; this directly addresses it.

Why fast adoption:
- Direct clinician benefit (time savings + cognitive relief).
- Hospital benefit (throughput + retention).
- Low regulatory risk (AI suggests; human signs; not decision-support).
- Low medico-legal risk (final note is clinician's).
- Patient-experience benefits (clinician makes eye contact, not typing).

Compare to clinical decision support: clinicians wary of being told what to do; liability unclear; workflow disruption. Hence slower adoption.

Ambient scribes ~one of the most successful clinical AI deployments. Multi-million dollar Series-B/C funding rounds (Abridge, Heidi Health, etc.). Major EHR partnerships (Epic AI, Microsoft Nuance).

slides.workedSolution: AI scribes save clinician 1-2 hr/day documentation. Address burnout directly. Don't change clinical decisions (regulatory + liability friendly). Clinicians experience direct value. Compare to decision support: liability + workflow friction = slower adoption. Scribes 2024 = largest active deployment of clinical AI. Major funding + EHR partnerships.

De-identifying notes for research
question.prompt: Your team wants to use 1M clinical notes for ML training. Walk through the de-identification + privacy compliance pipeline.
Explain in two or three sentences why clinical NLP is unusually difficult vs general-domain NLP.
question.rubric: Mentions that clinical text uses specialized vocabulary (abbreviations, jargon), heavy negation + temporality + uncertainty (must be detected correctly), high stakes (errors hurt patients), PHI requires de-identification + secure handling, regulatory + medico-legal context. Plus: clinical text is incomplete by design (clinicians document selectively). Foundation models help but require careful adaptation + evaluation.
